name: Murmur-3 Acoustic Suppression Field
description:
The Murmur-3 is a wearable acoustic suppression system produced by Tessera Corponation's civilian-adjacent defense division, originally marketed as an industrial noise-cancellation tool for hazardous work environments before security agencies recognized its obvious secondary application. The device consists of a chest-mounted processor unit roughly the size of a thick paperback, connected to a collar array of eight directional emitters that project a localized destructive interference field in a roughly 1.2-meter radius around the wearer. Sound generated within this bubble — footsteps, voices, equipment noise, the mechanical action of weapons — is sampled and countered in near-real-time, reducing it to a whisper-level floor before it can propagate outward.

The Murmur-3's processing latency is its defining technical character. Tessera's proprietary acoustic prediction algorithm anticipates sound events 11 milliseconds before full emission using gait analysis and motion sensors, which allows the system to suppress sharp transient sounds — impacts, clicks, the scrape of a boot on gravel — that would defeat purely reactive cancellation. This predictive layer is what separates the Murmur-3 from budget alternatives, which handle ambient noise adequately but fail on sudden sounds. The emitter collar is modular, with individual nodes replaceable in the field, and the whole rig can be worn under a jacket with minimal profile.

The device has found enthusiastic adoption among a broad range of users precisely because it sits in a legal gray area in most of GLMZ's administrative zones — classified as 'industrial hearing protection equipment' in its documentation, a fiction that Tessera maintains carefully and that local enforcement often finds convenient to accept.

specifications.suppression_radius: 1.2 meters nominal, 0.9 meters under heavy wind interference
specifications.sound_floor_reduction: Reduces internal sounds to ~18 dB SPL at field boundary
specifications.failure_mode: Harmonic feedback whine at ~3,200 Hz when two units operate within 4 meters of each other
specifications.form_factor: Chest processor unit + wearable collar, jacket-concealable

tactical_use: Standard use in infiltration scenarios where noise discipline is critical — clearing corridors with hard flooring, working near sleeping or distracted guards, conducting close-range surveillance conversations that can't be picked up by ambient mics. The harmonic feedback vulnerability is well-known and occasionally exploited by opposing operators to detect Murmur-equipped teams: sweeping a space with a paired Murmur unit will cause any active rig nearby to whine audibly. Teams using multiple units must stagger their activation.
cultural_context: The Murmur-3's 'industrial equipment' legal classification has made it the stealth tool of choice for operators who want deniability — it's something you can technically be caught with without immediately going to a black site. Mid-tier fixers treat it as standard kit, the same way a contractor treats a good multitool. There's a running joke in certain professional circles that Tessera's legal team is more dangerous than its R&D division.
known_users: union organizers operating in surveilled spaces
story_hooks: A critical meeting between two faction leaders was recorded despite both parties using Murmur-3 rigs — someone has either cracked Tessera's algorithm or there was a third party in the room that neither side knew about.

Tessera quietly recalls a specific production batch of Murmur-3 units, citing 'calibration errors.' The actual reason — that this batch has a firmware backdoor logging ambient audio to a Tessera server — hasn't leaked. Yet.

A player receives a Murmur-3 as payment for a job, only to discover the harmonic feedback vulnerability activates in a supposedly empty safehouse. Something else in the room is running a suppression field.

physical_description.visual_profile: A discrete tactical system consisting of a rectangular processor unit paired with a segmented collar array. The chest unit resembles a reinforced tech pack with subtle ergonomic curves; the collar appears as eight small hemispherical emitter pods distributed around a flexible retention band, designed to sit snug against the base of the neck and shoulders.
physical_description.dimensions: Processor unit: 19cm × 12cm × 4.5cm (thick paperback form factor). Collar array spans approximately 36cm circumference with individual emitters 2.8cm diameter.
physical_description.weight_description: 0.9kg total system weight — handheld in palm (processor alone), but worn distributed across chest and neck for balance. Light enough for all-day wear under tactical gear.
physical_description.primary_material: Processor housing: brushed titanium-composite with rubberized grip panels. Emitter collar: flexible smart-polymer backbone with ceramic acoustic nodes. Internal casing: anodized aluminum frame.
physical_description.finish: Matte anthracite with subtle oil-slick iridescence on emitter domes. Processor displays industrial mil-spec texture; collar band has soft-touch non-slip coating. Light weathering typical on field units.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: gunmetal gray and black. Accent: emerald status LEDs on processor face, faint cyan glow from active emitter nodes during operation. Manufacturer branding in matte silver.
physical_description.interface_elements: Processor unit features: small 3.8cm monochrome OLED status display, three recessed mechanical buttons (power, mode, calibrate), three 2mm diagnostic ports, battery indicator LED array (8-segment). Collar: no direct user interface — connects via flex-ribbon.
distinctive_features: Eight hemispherical emitter pods with barely-visible acoustic mesh intake ports
Modular quick-disconnect emitter nodes — field-replaceable without tools
Predictive algorithm indicator: pulsing blue LED when gait-lock is acquired
Minimal visible branding — deliberately understated 'industrial safety' aesthetic
Harmonic resonance venting ports on processor dorsal surface (prevent feedback whine buildup)
Flexible spine connecting collar to processor allows natural movement under clothing
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Tessera Corporation circular logo (small, rear-facing) and 'Murmur-3' designation in conservative sans-serif on processor. Legal gray-zone labeling: 'Industrial Acoustic Suppression System' with regulatory compliance marks (real or cosmetic).
physical_description.condition_typical: Field units show scuff marks on processor casing, slight discoloration around emitter domes from acoustic dampening material exposure. Battery indicator LED often dim (4-5 segment glow indicates worn power cell). Collar band may show creasing from being worn under jackets. Some units display faint scratches from rapid deployment.
